definition: Document Structuring is a subtask of Natural language generation, which involves deciding the order and grouping (for example into paragraphs) of sentences in a generated text.
details: It is closely related to the Content determination NLG task.
story: Think of a jazz musician who has heard so many solos that a new one simply falls out of their fingers. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. It makes new things by recombining everything it has ever seen. Creation, here, is memory recombined at speed. And that is Document structuring — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
